key_insight: A high-throughput DFT/minima-hopping search identified many new CuI-based ternary compounds that can function as p-type transparent conductors, and it extends valence-band design rules beyond oxides to halide systems.
engineering_relevance: These materials could enable transparent p-type layers for transparent electronics and tandem photovoltaic device stacks, where suitable hole-transporting transparent conductors are currently scarce.
method: Searched CuI-based X–Cu–I ternary space with the minima hopping method and density functional theory.
Filtered candidates by thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and light hole effective mass.
Revisited chemical modulation of the valence band descriptors to extract generalized design rules.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 58 candidate p-type TCMs, including 49 previously unreported compounds and 20 degenerate semiconductors with intrinsic hole carriers.
watch_item: Computational stability and electronic-structure screening do not guarantee synthesizability, long-term phase stability, or device-grade carrier mobility in real films.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
